skill.name: remix
skill.description: Builds, reviews, and refactors Remix 3 apps using the remix package and remix/* imports. Use for application structure, routing, middleware, data, auth, UI, browser interaction, and tests; not for implementing Remix framework packages.
skill.summary: Guide Remix 3 application changes using installed documentation, explicit routing, component patterns, and focused verification.
skill.author: remix-run

content.value_statement: Remix 3 application changes require version-specific APIs and component patterns that differ from React and Remix 2. This skill guides documentation checks, focused implementation, and behavior verification using existing application conventions.
actual_capabilities: Guides installed documentation lookup through the Remix index, package exports, READMEs, source, and types.
Explains explicit route contracts, router mapping, controllers, and typed URL generation.
Demonstrates Remix component state, event handlers, render functions, and handle.update().
Guides browser mounting and hydration checks for interactive server-rendered pages.
Recommends narrow application changes that preserve middleware order, runtime, package manager, and import conventions.
Guides tests, typechecking, rejection-path checks, secret isolation, and structural diagnostics.
limitations: Targets Remix 3 applications, not implementation of Remix framework packages.
Requires installed documentation and application context to verify exact APIs and imports.
Provides instructions and examples, not bundled automation, test suites, or application scaffolding.
Does not guarantee correctness or security; verification depends on available tools and project tests.

use_cases.title: Add a Typed Application Route
use_cases.description: Connect a new route contract, controller, and router mapping using installed APIs and the existing application structure.

use_cases.title: Review an Interactive Component
use_cases.description: Check local state, changing props, browser hydration, and event handling without applying React-specific assumptions.

use_cases.title: Verify a Structural Refactor
use_cases.description: Preserve runtime and middleware conventions while checking tests, typechecking, diagnostics, and failure paths.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the Application
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this Remix 3 app and explain its routes, router, and controllers. Check installed documentation before describing unfamiliar APIs.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a GET route for [feature] using this app's route contracts and controller conventions. Verify imports against installed documentation and run relevant checks.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Component Interaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [component] for stale props or missing browser interaction. Use Remix component patterns and verify both ordinary document behavior and the enhanced path.

prompt_templates.title: Review Access Control Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [change] for middleware order, access control, and browser-visible secrets. Test rejection paths and report unverified behavior. Run diagnostics after structural changes.

output_examples.input: Explain the request flow for the greeting route.
output: The route contract defines the GET endpoint and its name parameter.
The controller returns a plain greeting response using the matched parameter.
The router maps that contract to the controller and receives requests from the runtime adapter.
The same route contract generates links to the endpoint.

output_examples.input: Review a counter that appears on the page but does not respond to clicks.
output: Check that the component is mounted or hydrated in the browser.
Confirm that the click handler changes local state and requests another render.
Read changing props during rendering instead of capturing their initial values.
Verify the click interaction in a browser; rendered HTML alone does not establish interactivity.

best_practices: Check installed documentation before choosing APIs, imports, or component patterns.
Preserve existing application conventions and change the narrowest module responsible for the behavior.
Run relevant checks, exercise browser interactions, and report failure paths or behavior that remain unverified.
anti_patterns: Apply React hooks, Remix 2 conventions, or newer online APIs without checking the installed version.
Expose secrets or trusted server logic through browser-reachable modules.
Run destructive database commands or rewrite configuration solely to clear diagnostics.

faq.question: Which Remix version does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Remix 3 applications using the remix package and remix/* imports. Check installed documentation for exact APIs.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The report lists all three tools as supported. Available project access and verification tools determine what the assistant can check.

faq.question: Does it implement Remix framework packages?
faq.answer: No. Its scope is building, reviewing, and refactoring applications, not implementing framework packages.

faq.question: What happens if the installed documentation has no index?
faq.answer: Inspect package exports, matching READMEs, source, and types. Use existing application patterns to guide implementation.

faq.question: Does server-rendered HTML make components interactive?
faq.answer: No. Event handlers require browser mounting or hydration. Follow the installed interactivity guide and the application's browser-entry setup.

faq.question: Which verification steps does it recommend?
faq.answer: Run relevant tests and typechecking, exercise changed behavior, and test rejection paths. Run remix doctor after structural changes and review findings before fixes.
